sentences.text: Scientists estimated the weight of the holotype between 227 and 454 kilograms.
The preserved left dentary — the lower jawbone — features teeth with shield-shaped crowns.
The generic name Hippodraco combines the Greek word for 'horse' and the Latin word for 'dragon'.
The specific name scutodens references the shield-shaped crowns of the dentary teeth.
The holotype specimen UMNH VP 20208 was discovered in 2004 by Andrew R. C. Milner.
The genus was named in 2010 by Andrew T. McDonald, James I. Kirkland, Andrew R. C. Milner, Scott K. Madsen, Donald D. DeBlieux, Jennifer Cavin, and Lukas Panzarin.

Contemporaneous fauna included the ornithopod Cedrorestes, sauropods Cedarosaurus and Moabosaurus, theropods Martharaptor and Nedcolbertia, the nodosaurid Gastonia, and the giant dromaeosaurid Utahraptor.
Cladistic analyses from 2010 and 2011 recovered Hippodraco as a basal member of Styracosterna with Theiophytalia as its closest relative.
The parent group of Hippodraco is Styracosterna.
Hippodraco belongs to the class Ornithischia.
The holotype was found at Andrew's Site in the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation, dating to the Valanginian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
Hippodraco lived during the Valanginian stage, between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
